newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, China to step up economic cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Israel, China to step up economic cooperation.

text.p: Visiting Chinese Vice-Premier Li Lanquing agreed with Israeli Industry and Trade Minister Natan Sharansky to boost bilateral trade and economic cooperation, the industry ministry said on Wednesday.
Sharansky expressed disappointment at a meeting on Tuesday at the size of bilateral trade four years after Israel and China formally established diplomatic and trade relations.
Israeli exports to China reached $81 million last year, while Chinese exports to Israel were $160 million, the ministry said. It added that 70 percent of Israeli exports were in high technology.

The two sides agreed they would form set up joint committees to explore possible cooperation in agriculture, electronics, medical equipment and telecommunications. The committees will investigate Chinese needs and identify relevant Israeli companies.
Li said the two countries would also pursue joint projects in countries neighbouring China.
Earlier in the week the two countries signed a customs agreement establishing a framework for coordination between their customs agencies.
